title: CapCut Review (2026): Free Video Editor, Auto Captions, Pro Price
meta_description: Plain-English CapCut review for small business owners: what the free plan does, what Pro costs, auto captions, and the license terms to read first.
summary: CapCut is a free video editor for phone, desktop, and web that writes captions for you from what's said in the video. Pro is listed at $19.99 and adds 1,200 AI credits a month. The catch for a business: some templates and music are licensed for personal use only, so check the "commercial" mark before you post an ad.
one_liner: Free video editor that writes your captions for you from the audio.
why_care:
Short videos with captions are how a lot of small businesses show up on TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts. CapCut listens to your video, types the captions, and lets you trim, resize, and post without paying an editor.

If you don't post video for your business, skip it.
good_for: Put captions on a 60-second shop tour so people watching with the sound off can follow it.
Trim a long phone video down to the 30 seconds that matter.
Resize one video for TikTok, YouTube, and a square post; CapCut keeps the main subject in the frame.
Translate captions into another language for customers who speak it (check names and terms before posting).
Find a clip in your footage by searching for a person, object, or something that was said (desktop app).
Turn a written script into a draft video with the Script to video tool (paid AI features; results unverified).
how_to_use:
Step 1: Sign up free at capcut.com and download the desktop app (Windows 10 recommended, or macOS 10.14 and up), or use the web version.

Step 2: Drag your video onto the timeline. Go to Text, pick Auto captions, and click Generate.

Step 3: Read every caption line and fix names and prices. Then click Export and pick your resolution, or share straight to TikTok or YouTube.
what_youll_get:
A captioned, trimmed video in the size each social site wants, made in one free app. CapCut says its captions are "almost perfect." That is CapCut's claim, not ours, and its own help text tells you to check names, terms, and timing before you publish.

We have not run our own tests for this review.
missing: CapCut's pricing page says its prices are "for reference only." You see your final price, taxes, and offers only after you sign in.
AI features run on credits: Pro lists 1,200 a month, Ultra 8,645. Run out and you buy more.
Some templates, stickers, and music are licensed for personal, non-commercial use only. Only items marked "commercial" can go in business content, per CapCut's license terms.
When you submit content, CapCut's terms give its US operator a worldwide, royalty-free license to use it to run and develop the service.
What the free plan leaves out (export quality, watermarks) is not spelled out on the pages we checked [CHECK].
verdict: Captions and quick social edits for $0, which covers what most small businesses need from it. The license fine print on templates and music is the reason it isn't ranked higher: read the "commercial" mark before anything goes in an ad.
price_free: Free plan, $0: free templates and basic editing tools. Auto captions are described as free on CapCut's caption page. Pro has a 7-day free trial, no credit card required, per CapCut (may vary by region).
price_paid: Listed in USD: Pro $19.99 (1,200 AI credits a month, 1 TB storage). Ultra $79 (8,645 AI credits a month). Teams $12.49 (per seat, adds Brand Kit). Billing period is not shown before sign-in [CHECK: likely monthly]. CapCut says prices are for reference only. Checked Nov 23, 2026.
when_to_use:
* You post short videos for your business on TikTok, Reels, or YouTube.
* You want captions without typing them.
* You shoot on your phone and need fast trims and resizing.
* You don't want to pay for editing software until you know you'll keep posting.
when_to_skip:
* You don't make video for your business.
* You need every template and song cleared for paid ads without checking each one.
* Your company rules don't allow uploading client footage to a service with a broad content license.
* You record screen walkthroughs, not social clips. A screen recorder fits that job better.
missing_text:
Here's how the money works, as listed on CapCut's pricing page.

Plan	Listed price (USD)	What you get
Free	$0	Free templates, basic editing tools
Pro	$19.99	1,200 AI credits a month, premium templates, Pro features, 1 TB storage
Ultra	$79	8,645 AI credits a month, everything in Pro plus extra AI features
Teams	$12.49	Pro features for every seat, 1,200 AI credits per seat, Brand Kit

The catches:

* CapCut says these prices are "for reference only." Sign in to see what you'd actually pay, plus taxes.
* The billing period is not shown on the public page [CHECK]. Paid plans can auto-renew until you cancel, per CapCut's terms.
* AI video generation uses credits, and you can buy more. Watch the meter.

Bottom line: Start free. Only pay for Pro if you're using the AI tools every week and the free captions and edits aren't enough.
privacy:
CapCut in the US is run by TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC, per its Terms of Service (updated April 15, 2026). When you submit content, you give it and its partners a worldwide, royalty-free, sub-licensable, perpetual license to use that content for operating, developing, and providing the service, subject to your settings.

Don't upload client footage or anything confidential unless you're fine with those terms. We did not read CapCut's full Privacy Policy for this review [CHECK].
alternatives:
* Descript — If you'd rather edit video by editing the transcript, like a Word doc [CHECK: not reviewed here].
* Canva AI — If you already make your flyers in Canva and want simple video in the same place. Read our Canva AI review.
* Loom — If your videos are screen walkthroughs for staff or customers, not social posts. Read our Loom review.
